title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the surrounding notes on the 'Galois theory of motives': X is a scheme of finite type over a number field k. For each point α of X there are fibre functors (realizations) on the category of motives over X, with values in categories T_α(Λ) of Λ-modules for Λ = Z, R, C, ... with extra structure. This page treats the archimedean case: an embedding of the residue field k(α) into C, i.e. a complex place, written ᾱ.

The page opens mid-sentence: '..., i.e. the completion of k(α) is ≅ R' (canonical isomorphism). This is the case where α is a real place. Then the integral Betti realization ξ_{α,Z} is also defined from the archimedean structure on k(α). But it depends on the choices in the algebraic closure of k(α), that is, on the choice of complex embedding. The group Gal(C/R) = {1, τ} acts on the lattice ξ_{α,Z} by an involution. This is what is now called F_∞, the 'infinite Frobenius'.

A bracketed remark: this operation is the conjugation induced by the semilinear (½-linear) involution of the complex realization ξ_{ᾱ,∞} that corresponds to the Z-structure. In this setting 'there is no question, for example, of a Hodge variation'. Hodge filtrations are deliberately left out at this stage.

The invariants attached to a real point are:
- a real realization ξ_{α,∞} ∈ T_α(R);
- an integral lattice ξ_{ᾱ,Z} ∈ T_α(Z);
- a complex realization ξ_{ᾱ,∞} ∈ T_α(C);
- comparison isomorphisms ξ_{ᾱ,∞} ≅(can) ξ_{α,∞}⊗_R C ≅ ξ_{ᾱ,Z}⊗_Z C.

Final remarks:
- Unlike at finite places, π_1(X) does not act on ξ_{α,Z}; at an archimedean point the only 'decomposition group' is Gal(C/R), acting through τ when α is real.
- On the complex realization ξ_{ᾱ,∞} there are, in addition to τ, semilinear actions of Aut_{k(α)}(K), where K is a big algebraically closed field (C). These come from the fact that the realization can be defined algebraically over k(α), so field automorphisms act σ-semilinearly.

Purpose: to list, place by place, the 'Galois-type' structures on the realizations of a motive. The archimedean place contributes Gal(C/R) and the real/integral comparison data, as the analogue of the decomposition and inertia data at finite places. This feeds into the description of the motivic Galois group and its local pieces.
errors: The semilinear action of Aut_{k(α)}(C) cannot be defined on ξ_{ᾱ,Z}⊗C via the Betti lattice. Non-continuous automorphisms of C do not preserve Betti lattices or transport singular cohomology. The action only makes sense on the algebraically defined (de Rham-type) realization tensored up to C, transported through the comparison isomorphism. The page does not make this distinction explicit.

Notation is loose: the subscripts α and ᾱ are used somewhat interchangeably (e.g. ξ_{α,Z} vs ξ_{ᾱ,Z}). The identification ξ_{ᾱ,∞} ≅ ξ_{α,∞}⊗_R C presupposes that α is real, which is only stated in the truncated first line.

ideas.what: Complex conjugation Gal(C/R) acting by an involution on the integral Betti realization at a real point; the archimedean analogue of the decomposition group.
ideas.modern_name: Infinite Frobenius F_∞ on Betti cohomology / real structure of the Betti realization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Serre's and Grothendieck's motivic yoga; systematized by Deligne ('Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales', 1979)

ideas.what: Package of real, integral and complex realizations at an archimedean point, with canonical comparison isomorphisms ξ_C ≅ ξ_R⊗C ≅ ξ_Z⊗C.
ideas.modern_name: Betti/de Rham comparison and real structure; the archimedean component of the realization system of a motive
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1979; Jannsen, 'Mixed motives and algebraic K-theory' (realization categories)

ideas.what: Semilinear action of field automorphisms Aut_{k(α)}(C) on the complex realization.
ideas.modern_name: σ-semilinear action of Aut(C/k) on de Rham ⊗ C, used in absolute Hodge cycles

ideas.what: Remark that at an archimedean point π_1(X) plays no role; only τ acts.

missed.claim: Already in the 1965 Galois-theory-of-motives notes, Grothendieck records the archimedean realization data that Deligne later made standard in 1979–82. This includes the F_∞ involution on the Betti lattice, the R-, Z- and C-comparisons, and a semilinear action of Aut(C/k(α)) on the complex realization. It is a documentary precursor of the absolute-Hodge setting, not a new result.
missed.quote: les opérations de Aut_{k(α)} E(k) qui sont ½ linéaires
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents that the semilinear Aut(C) action on realizations, central to absolute Hodge cycles, was part of Grothendieck's motivic Galois framework in 1965.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard (F_∞, comparison isomorphisms, semilinear Aut(C) action). The page is of mild historical interest as an early, explicit listing of archimedean realization data and of semilinear field-automorphism actions in Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois notes.
transcription_corrections: The first line probably reads: 'C, i.e. \widehat{k(α)} ≅ R (isom. can.), alors ξ_{α,Z} est aussi défini ...'. The bar likely denotes completion, not algebraic closure.
In the last line 'Aut_{k(α)} E(k)' is uncertain. The subscript k(α) sits under 'Aut'; the object is probably a big field K (= C) or an extension of it, so read 'Aut_{k(α)}(K)'.
The garbled phrase 'il n'y a pas question par exemple d'une variation [?] Hodge' is plausibly '... d'une structure de Hodge'. In context it means Hodge data are not yet considered.
